questions.stem: Find the cross product of vector A = <2, 3, 4> and vector B = <-1, 5, 6>.
questions.solution: The cross product of two vectors A and B is calculated as follows: A x B = (Ay * Bz - Az * By)i - (Ax * Bz - Az * Bx)j + (Ax * By - Ay * Bx)k. Plugging in the values, we get: A x B = (3 * 6 - 4 * 5)i - (2 * 6 - 4 * (-1))j + (2 * 5 - 3 * (-1))k = <-7, 10, 7>. Therefore, the correct answer is A.
questions.explanation: The cross product results in a vector perpendicular to both input vectors. The formula involves multiplying corresponding components and taking differences, then applying the right-hand rule for orientation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be swapping the order of multiplication or forgetting to negate one of the terms when calculating the components of the resulting vector.
